rv.q: As a work of subversive mischief, 'A Mirror' is a triumph, a gloriously ballsy biting of the hand that feeds...
...actually very funny, and also a structural marvel.
It’s ingenious and often very funny, as the cast play with levels of reality.
Yet with so many arguments and little action, it’s a bit too clever for its own good.
'A Mirror' is a timely production packed with intrigue and passion.
Director Jeremy Herrin has got his cast to play-act this set-up with total conviction, but it is nevertheless a hollow one...
A compelling story, but unnecessarily convoluted at times.

It has the potential to be gripping, dramatic and engaging but its structure, stereotypical characters (a drunken established author, a nervous wannabe writer, a young attractive female assistant, and a manic ambitious director) and unbelievable interactions makes it very hard work.

cn.t: Holcroft's clever meta-theatrical satire about censorship divides critics with its play-within-a-play structure. Many praise its mischievous concept and brilliant finale, but others find it confusing and tedious before reaching its payoff.
